pages.text: Rain poured down. The roof edges stuck out over the road, making shelter underneath called the eaves. Taro stood under the eaves on this side, and Mumu stood on the other side. Only one road lay between them, but the rain made their voices hard to hear.
"Let's go to the stream as soon as it stops!" Taro shouted. Mumu nodded.
The rain grew heavier, drumming on the roofs. Both friends stepped farther under the eaves.
The rain grew a little lighter. Taro shouted, "Let's go now!"
Mumu heard no words, even with such sharp ears. The rain had swallowed them all.
Mumu spread out a mat. "It must be a while yet." Then Mumu flopped down.
Taro waited under the eaves. Mumu did not come. "Why aren't they coming?"
The rain stopped. Taro crossed the road. Mumu was sleeping soundly!
Taro shook Mumu. "Why are you asleep?" "I couldn't hear a thing you said!"
Rain poured again. They sat side by side under the eaves, with stream water dripping from their feet. Taro shouted something, and Mumu promptly flopped down.
